subject: flying fish
title: A Fish That Stayed Airborne for 45 Seconds, Filmed

scenes.text: A fish stayed in the air for 45 seconds. That is a world record.
Flying fish launch by swimming up fast and beating the tail furiously.
scenes.keywords: flying fish leaping out of water

scenes.text: Then they spread huge fins and glide. Some glides cover about 400 metres.
They can rise up to eight metres above the waves, higher than a two-story house.
And they can glide again and again, up to 12 times in a row.
Why leave the water? Fast predators like dolphinfish are chasing them. The sky is their escape.

description:
A flying fish was filmed gliding for 45 seconds in Japan in 2008, a Guinness World Record.
They launch with a furious tail beat, glide up to about 400 metres, and can rise up to eight metres above the sea.
Which animal would you most like to see fly? Tell us.
first_comment: The record was filmed from a ferry near Yakushima island in Japan in 2008. Would you rather glide like a flying fish or swim like a dolphin?
